exact_inputs.scope: BC2-01A establishes all140[92..139] as the 48 exceptional pairing coordinates in Stoll runtime order.

construction_order_algorithm: Construct L=Q(i,s) with i^2=-1 and s^2=2, P^6_L with coordinate order [a1,a2,a3,b1,b2,b3,c], and the four Stoll cuboid equations.
Set S to the resulting projective surface and evaluate pts := Points(SingularSubscheme(S)); Stoll asserts #pts=48.
Stoll constructs Cs=C1s cat C2s cat C3s with #Cs=92, then all140 as the 92 curve classes followed by the 48 exceptional divisors represented by pts.
Therefore runtime exceptional index k in 0..47 is exactly pts[k+1], and its all140 index is 92+k (0-based), equivalently 93+k (1-based).
MatCP[j,k+1] is the exact incidence predicate pts[k+1] in Cpts[j]; the same pts indexed set is used by Position(pts, transformed_point) for automorphism/Galois permutations.
For persistence, normalize each pts[k+1] by dividing all seven homogeneous coordinates by the first nonzero coordinate in [a1,a2,a3,b1,b2,b3,c].

claims.claim: For every k=0..47, runtime exceptional index k is the exceptional divisor over the singular projective point pts[k+1] from the same Stoll indexed set; its all140 coordinate is 92+k.
